newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dredging, housing lift Ballast Ned H1 net.
newsitem.headline: Dredging, housing lift Ballast Ned H1 net.

text.p: Dutch builder Ballast Nedam on Wednesday said first-half profits rose by almost 10 percent, driven by healthy dredging demand and increased activity at its Dutch housing and general building units.
"The healthy trend on the dredging market, a number of foreign projects and the Dutch utility and housing units contributed particularly to the result," Ballast said.
But it said results at Ballast Wiltshier, its U.K. arm, had lagged expectations as the uptrend on the British building market had not yet translated into improved margins.

Ballast Nedam, which is 48 percent owned by Hochtief AG of Germany, earlier reported first-half net profit up 3.0 million guilders at 35 million and repeated its forecast of at least five percent profit growth for the full year.
Turnover rose to 1.7 billion guilders from a year-earlier 1.5 billion.
For the full year Ballast is forecasting turnover will rise to more than four billion guilders from 3.8 billion in 1996.
"Over the coming years a gradual growth in turnover and results is expected in view of the development of the order portfolio and market trends," Ballast said.
It said the size of its order book remained unchanged from end-1996 at 3.6 billion guilders, adding that it was in advanced talks on a number of "interesting new projects".
"The size, spread and composition of the order portfolio is satisfactory," Ballast added.
In a separate statement, the builder said it had booked orders worth over one billion guilders at home and abroad over the second 1997 quarter.
These included the construction of a string of Dutch outlets for British-based chemists' chain Boots, starting with shops in Rotterdam, Maastricht and Breda, it said.

Other projects include dredging work on the new harbour being built in Tanjung Pelepas in Malaysia, land reclamation for a container terminal in Hamburg and work on the expansion of a power plant in Buenos Aires under contract for Mitsubishi Heavy Industries, Ballast said.
